lines.text: In this world, everybody believes in God.
Huss... huss... huss...
Problem is, there's zero proof. Not a footprint. Not a receipt.
Scientists tried. Telescopes, microscopes, one guy even licked a meteorite. Nothing.
But nobody could prove He didn't exist either. Total stalemate. For centuries.
Then the philosophers had a breakthrough. They called it...
the Burger Wager.
If you believe in God and you're wrong? You lose nothing.
If you believe and you're right? Infinite rewards. Forever.
But if you don't believe, and He's real? Infinite punishment. Forever.
Infinite heaven, versus a little effort. The math was perfect.
And it worked. Ninety-nine point nine percent of the world didn't just believe. They went full religious.
Prayer apps. Church drive-throughs. Babies baptized before they could even blink.
And then there was me. The last non-believer on Earth.
Because the argument just didn't sit right with me.
You can't flip a belief switch because someone offered you a prize. I'm not a robot.
You can bet on a team you think will lose. Doesn't mean you believe they'll win.
But everyone was worried about me.
Sweetie, we pray for you every single night.
Bro, they're gonna roast you. Literally.
And honestly, I didn't wanna burn either.
So I did the research. Every counterargument. Every loophole.
I couldn't beat the odds. Infinity always wins.
So I gave in. I believed.
And you know what? It wasn't so bad.
My life had purpose. I was happy. I had a church family that brought me casseroles.
Sixty years passed. And then, I died.
I opened my eyes in a white room.
I was right! He's real! The wager paid off!
Then I saw everyone else. Being thrown into the fire.
My pastor. My mom. The guy who invented the wager.
I left no evidence. On purpose.
I don't reward belief. I reward warranted belief.
You had no reason to believe in me. So you shouldn't have.
Turns out, it was never a two-option bet.
There were infinite possible gods, wanting infinite possible things. We only thought of one.
We all burned.
And the worst part? I was right the first time.
